key_insight: DiffEEG learns generic EEG representations from large-scale unlabeled data using diffusion pre-training, then improves rare seizure detection with reinforcement learning optimized directly for F1-score.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical path to clinically useful EEG seizure monitoring when labels are scarce and class imbalance is severe, while keeping the model compact at 9.6M parameters.
method: 1D U-Net with multi-head self-attention for denoising diffusion pre-training
Pre-train self-supervised on 1.3M unlabeled EEG segments from TUHSZ
Use policy-gradient reinforcement learning to fine-tune a decision layer for F1-aware seizure detection
evidence_signal: Under patient-wise Leave-One-Fold-Out evaluation on 279 patients, DiffEEG reports 61% accuracy and 59% F1 for 4-class seizure subtyping, and 81% accuracy with 85% weighted F1 for binary detection at 6.7% seizure prevalence.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on patient-wise validation and a specific corpus, so generalization to other hospitals, montages, or recording conditions still needs external testing.
paper_title: DiffEEG: A Self-Supervised Denoising Diffusion Model for Learning EEG Generic Representations
